label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 8
knowledgePattern: Test possible exponential rules against every required input
solution:
For I, any b>a gives b0=1, b2>a2 and b−1<a−1, so I can hold. For II, 0<b<a gives b2<a2, contradicting the required value at 2.

For III, choose k>1. Then ak>a and akx=(ak)x has the form already checked in I.

For IV, f(2)=b4>a2 would require b>a>1. But f(−1)=b<a−1<1 requires the opposite. Hence IV is impossible. Exactly I and III might be true. Answer C.

hints.title: Make a table of the three inputs
hints.body: For each proposed formula, work out f(0), f(2) and f(−1). Put these in three columns next to the formula.
hints.recap: A negative exponent means a reciprocal; squaring a negative input is a different operation.
hints.pitfall: In the last formula, square the input before using it as the exponent.
hints.pause: Fill in the table before deciding which statements might work.

recall.reminder: A negative exponent means a reciprocal; squaring a negative input is a different operation.

hints.title: Can one choice pass all three checks?
hints.body: Compare each row with the three given conditions. Try to choose b or k so that the whole row works. If two checks demand incompatible values, reject that row.
hints.recap: “Might be true” needs one allowed choice that works, not every choice.
hints.pitfall: Do not choose a different b or k for each column.
hints.pause: Show a working parameter choice or a contradiction for each row.
